b:
The moth
playing
in the lamplight
says
it does not want the dawn

But she
keeps a fast
for the dawn

When dusk falls
with many desires
a hired husband
waits at her door

In her house
where money never runs short
every single day
a wedding night
without a wedding thread

When the lust has cooled
the wounds on a body without clothes,
covered up again in despair,
tell a thousand stories

The man who desired her
until even shame ran out
will tomorrow
call her a whore
and turn
the other way

Even if she changes her path
there, blocking it,
tomorrow's Dushasanas
will be waiting
to strip her of her sari

And for her
no Krishna
is coming there

She is born with the dawn,
she,
for another night
note: The "wedding thread" is the thali, the sacred thread tied at a Tamil wedding. Dushasana is the Mahabharata prince who tried to disrobe Draupadi in the royal court; Krishna saved her by making her sari endless.
